at_an_a_row.where_it_fires: NOT on the a-row itself: the a-rows carry Q = 256 pads against 243 distinct sampled nodes, so their Cauchy block is square and nonsingular and the pads absorb the moved target exactly.  It fires on the FOUR rows below -- b_re, b_im, u_re, u_im, at that one column and at no other -- because b is the residue of q and u the residue of the proximity vector: absorbing the move on the a-row moves the verifier's per-column identity at that node, and the capture's own b and u entries there contradict it.
